## Introduction

The past decade has witnessed an unprecedented surge in quantum computing research, driven by breakthroughs in qubit engineering, error‑correction protocols, and algorithmic development. Major technology firms and national laboratories have launched roadmaps targeting quantum advantage for specific tasks such as cryptography, materials simulation, and optimization. The rapid scaling of superconducting and trapped‑ion platforms, combined with cloud‑based quantum services, has democratized access and accelerated interdisciplinary collaborations across physics, computer science, and engineering.

## Challenges

Despite the momentum, decoherence remains the principal obstacle to building reliable quantum processors. Interactions with the environment cause loss of quantum coherence on timescales that are often shorter than gate operations, leading to errors that degrade computational fidelity. Mitigating decoherence requires advances in materials purity, isolation techniques, and robust quantum error‑correction codes. Moreover, scaling up qubit counts amplifies control‑line crosstalk and thermal management issues, demanding innovative architectures and cryogenic engineering solutions.
